ct_parking_lot_wall.blurb: A short cliff at Ross Rocks in Killingly, in the northeast corner of Connecticut, rising directly above the trailhead lot so there is almost no walk. The face stands roughly 30 to 40 feet tall and is split by cracks with face climbing between them. Of its dozen routes, most are traditional leads and a handful are normally top-roped. Difficulty starts around 5.5, which gives newer leaders a few comfortable lines, then climbs through the 5.8 to 5.10 range to a couple of hard routes at 5.11 and 5.12. Grades here have a reputation for feeling stiff, and rock quality across the cliffs is uneven, so expect to test holds.

ks_toadstool_pinnacle.blurb: A small bouldering zone inside Shroomie's Boulder Field, part of the Lost City of Critzer in eastern Kansas. The centerpiece is a limestone toadstool with an overhanging cap, and a little boulder sits on the south edge of it. All twelve problems are boulder problems, weighted toward the easy end: mostly V0 to V2, then a few harder ones from V3 up to V5. The wider field is made of mushroom-shaped limestone formations about 8 to 12 feet tall, so the landings are moderate. A good stop for a short session on the way to or from the neighbouring walls.
